content.title: About
content.content: Rice squares are dry, crunchy cereal pieces made from whole grain rice, formed into small square shapes. They are often used in children's meals and as a quick snack. The product is gluten‑free and suitable for vegetarians.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first rice squares appeared in Japan in the 1970s as an alternative to corn‑based snacks.
Large manufacturers use extrusion technology, which preserves most of the rice's nutrients.
Rice squares are frequently fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.
Unlike many breakfast cereals, they contain no added sugar unless specified on the label.
There is a low‑salt version designed for younger children.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Rice squares contain virtually no fat, making them a light snack option.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: They provide slowly digestible carbohydrates that give sustained energy.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Fortified versions help replenish iron stores, especially for vegetarians.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 support metabolic processes.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to rice.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Consuming large amounts can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Some varieties contain added salt; those limiting sodium should choose unsalted versions.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Fortified products may contain artificial flavors and colorings that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rice squares can be eaten dry as a snack, added to yogurt, milk, or fruit smoothies. They are also used in baby foods, mixed into porridge or purees.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight package. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to prevent moisture absorption.
